channel.title: Resilient Waters
channel.description: Climate Resilience, Water & Ecosystems Explained Simply — a research blog by Isaac Bright Addo on climate adaptation, water security, ecohydrology and sustainability.

item.title: River Ecosystem Health Indicators
item.description: A river cannot tell you how it is doing in words — but it leaves signs. Water chemistry, the insects and fish that live in it, and the shape of its banks and flow together show whether a river ecosystem is healthy or quietly failing.

item.title: Watershed Management for Sustainable Development
item.description: A watershed is the whole land area that drains to one river. Managing water at that scale — land, forests, farms, towns and allocation together — is how the pieces in this series become a plan.

item.title: How Forests Regulate Water Cycles
item.description: Forests are not just places that receive rain — they help make it, store it, clean it and release it slowly. A plain-language guide to how forests regulate the water cycle, and what changes when they are lost.

item.title: What Is Eco-Hydrology? A Beginner's Guide
item.description: Eco-hydrology is the science of how water and living systems shape each other. A plain-language guide to the idea behind wetlands, forests and rivers that keep water clean, steady and alive.

item.title: The Role of Wetlands in Climate Resilience
item.description: Wetlands slow floods, clean water, store carbon and keep rivers alive in drought. Why the landscape's own water keepers are among the strongest defences against a changing climate.

item.title: Water Conservation Strategies for Drought-Prone Regions
item.description: Rainwater harvesting, smart irrigation, community water management and smart policy: how drought-prone regions are learning to make every drop count.

item.title: How Cities Are Adapting to Extreme Heat
item.description: Urban heat islands make cities dangerously hotter than the countryside around them. Green roofs, cool pavements and urban forests — and lessons from Singapore, Vienna and Los Angeles.

item.title: 10 Nature-Based Solutions Fighting Climate Change
item.description: Mangroves, wetlands, forests, peatlands and more: ten ways working with nature protects communities from floods, heat, drought and rising seas — and the honest challenges that come with them.

item.title: What Is Climate Adaptation and Why Does It Matter?
item.description: Climate adaptation means adjusting to the changes already under way — hotter days, heavier rain, longer droughts. What it is, how it differs from mitigation, real examples, and why every community needs it.
